name: Elbow Extension
definition: A strict open-chain isolation movement in which the elbow extends while a reviewed upper-arm posture is held and shoulder, torso, and lower-body motion do not create the repetition. Triceps is the sole primary on every record. The roster admits reviewed cable, dumbbell, barbell, and exact Life Fitness Pro 2 PSTE selectorized fixtures. The PSTE supports both upper arms on a pad, aligns the elbows with the pivots, and guides self-adjusting handles; its manual does not report forearm orientation or wrist posture, so both remain unreported. Finger flexors author the static implement hold and extensor carpi radialis supplies mechanics-derived wrist counter-control. Scapular support, held-forearm control, and stabilizer assignments are bounded mechanics applications rather than variables directly compared in the triceps trials. Other machine topologies remain outside this contract.

variantAxes.description: Whether the loaded hand moves freely or remains fixed to the environment.
The whole-body posture used by the reviewed elbow-extension fixture.
The external surface directly supporting the torso; a seat without back contact is not torso support.
Whether external posterior support limits scapular translation along the thorax; this does not name a dynamic scapular action.
The external surface supporting the forearm independently of torso support.
Whether an external pad supports the upper arms while the elbows move.
The source-reported hip contact used during the fixture; most reviewed free-weight and cable sources do not report one.
The torso-relative upper-arm posture held while the elbow moves: anatomical side, 90 degrees of sagittal flexion, or 180-degree overhead flexion. A held posture does not add a shoulder prime action.
The dynamic elbow action that creates the concentric repetition.
Whether the radioulnar angle is held or changes deliberately during the repetition.
The radioulnar posture held during elbow extension, independent of implement wording and dynamic forearm rotation.
Whether wrist angle is held or changes deliberately during the repetition.
The reviewed wrist posture held during elbow extension; neutral is an authoring target rather than a zero-error measurement claim.
The task performed by the fingers while the elbow creates the repetition.
The reviewed load-to-hand interface used by the cable or dumbbell fixture.

How the reviewed task creates elbow-extension resistance without implying a guided external path. highCablePushdown records Villalba's at-side pulley setup; overheadCableExtension identifies Maeo's 180-degree cable task but deliberately does not claim an unreported pulley height or cable angle; gravityLoadedDumbbell records the Alves fixtures.
Cable-stack values are comparable only on the same cable station and attachment fixture; dumbbell fixtures omit this field.
A discriminator that keeps the two reviewed seated topologies from forming unsupported combinations.
The exact commercial machine whose setup and stack history are reviewed.
The explicitly reported torso inclination for a fixture.
The explicitly reported upper-arm relationship to the torso.
The explicitly reported bilateral hand spacing.
Whether rails or a lever machine constrain the external load path; cable direction alone is not a fixed path.
Whether hip, knee, or ankle drive contributes to elbow extension.

exerciseRules.description: A cable extension uses the directly reported single handle or preserves the overhead study's unreported interface rather than inventing a dumbbell interface.
Every reviewed dumbbell extension uses a dumbbell handle rather than a cable interface.
The reviewed standing branch uses an unsupported free-scapula cable setup with the upper arm at the side or overhead and the forearm supinated or pronated.
Every seated record declares which of the two reviewed seated topologies it uses.
The reviewed seated dumbbell record remains unsupported, overhead, neutral-forearm, and free-path.
The machine branch is only the seated Life Fitness Pro 2 PSTE selectorized lever with supported upper arms and an exact-fixture load history.
The reviewed cable, dumbbell, and barbell fixtures do not constrain the implement to a lever path.
The exact PSTE identity cannot be attached to a free-weight or cable record.
The exact Life Fitness Pro 2 PSTE seated topology cannot be attached to the unsupported dumbbell fixture.
Standing and lying records cannot claim a seated topology.

Both reviewed lying extensions hold the upper arm at 90 degrees of shoulder flexion; the dumbbell study reports bench support and neutral forearms while the barbell study leaves its support and forearm orientation unreported.
The pronated orientation is admitted only in the directly reviewed standing at-side cable pushdown.
The reviewed overhead setups use lower trapezius as the categorical scapular stabilizer.
Every admitted at-side extension is one of the reviewed high-cable pushdown fixtures.
Maeo reports the overhead cable task but not its attachment, pulley height, or cable angle, so the record preserves an unreported interface rather than manufacturing one.
The at-side and bench-supported non-overhead setups use middle trapezius as the categorical scapular stabilizer.
Standing and unsupported seated extensions require explicit spine and pelvis stability with obliques assigned as a stabilizer.
The single cable handle remains a one-arm fixture and omits bilateral attachment fields.
The source-unreported overhead cable interface remains a one-arm fixture.
The reviewed dumbbell extensions remain one-arm fixtures.
The unreported barbell interface belongs only to Brandao et al.'s bilateral lying triceps press and preserves every fixture detail the paper does not report.
The rope attachment pins the upright bilateral neutral-grip pushdown while omitting straight-bar-only geometry.
The straight-bar attachment belongs only to the reviewed bilateral pronated pushdown.

execution.startingPosition: Stand at a high cable, and hold a single handle with the working palm facing up. Compare the entered load only on this same cable station and attachment.
execution.movement: Straighten the elbow from about 90 degrees.
execution.endpoint: End the pushdown with your elbow fully straight.
execution.returnPhase: Return under control without moving the shoulder or rotating the forearm.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep the upper arm alongside your torso and the wrist straight.
execution.supportAndPosture: Stand upright with your feet planted and your trunk braced.
disqualifyingCompensations: Letting the upper arm drift away from the torso turns the pushdown into an overhead extension.
Rotating the forearm during the push turns the palm-up pushdown into a palm-down pushdown.
execution.sideOrDirection: Finish the set with one arm, then repeat with the other arm.

execution.startingPosition: Stand at a high cable, and hold a single handle with the working palm facing down. Compare the entered load only on this same cable station and attachment.
execution.movement: Straighten the elbow from about 90 degrees.
execution.endpoint: End the pushdown with your elbow fully straight.
execution.returnPhase: Return under control without moving the shoulder or rotating the forearm.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep the upper arm alongside your torso and the wrist straight.
execution.supportAndPosture: Stand upright with your feet planted and your trunk braced.
disqualifyingCompensations: Letting the upper arm drift away from the torso turns the pushdown into an overhead extension.
Rotating the forearm during the push turns the palm-down pushdown into a palm-up pushdown.
execution.sideOrDirection: Finish the set with one arm, then repeat with the other arm.

execution.startingPosition: Stand with one arm overhead and the palm facing up while the cable pulls against you. Compare the entered load only on this same cable station and attachment.
execution.movement: Straighten the elbow from about 90 degrees.
execution.endpoint: End the extension with your elbow fully straight.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep your upper arm, wrist, torso, and lower body still.
execution.supportAndPosture: Stand upright with your feet planted and your trunk braced.
disqualifyingCompensations: Dropping the upper arm to your side turns the overhead extension into a pushdown.
Arching the back to move the handle turns the overhead extension into a back-assisted press.
execution.sideOrDirection: Finish the set with one arm, then repeat with the other arm.

exercises.name: Seated Single-Arm Overhead Dumbbell Triceps Extension

execution.startingPosition: Sit upright without back support, and hold one dumbbell overhead with your palm facing inward.
execution.movement: Bend the elbow to lower the dumbbell.
execution.endpoint: End the lowering with the dumbbell at the bottom of the repetition.
execution.returnPhase: Straighten the elbow as far as you can without turning the forearm.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep your upper arm and torso still.
execution.supportAndPosture: Support yourself on the seat with your trunk braced and no back support.
disqualifyingCompensations: Dropping the upper arm to your side turns the overhead extension into a pushdown.
Turning the forearm while straightening turns the extension into a forearm rotation.
execution.sideOrDirection: Finish the set with one arm, then repeat with the other arm.

execution.startingPosition: Lie on your back on a bench with one dumbbell held over your chest, your palm facing inward, and your upper arm pointing straight up.
execution.movement: Bend the elbow to lower the dumbbell.
execution.endpoint: End the lowering with the dumbbell at the bottom of the repetition.
execution.returnPhase: Straighten the elbow as far as you can.
execution.supportAndPosture: Support your torso fully on the bench.
disqualifyingCompensations: Letting the upper arm fall toward your torso turns the lying extension into a close-grip press.
Tilting the upper arm back overhead turns the lying extension into an overhead extension.
execution.sideOrDirection: Finish the set with one arm, then repeat with the other arm.

execution.startingPosition: Lie on your back with your torso supported and hold one barbell with both hands above the chest. Record the total bar-and-plate load and use a comfortable grip.
execution.movement: Keep both upper arms at 90 degrees of shoulder flexion while bending both elbows together.
execution.endpoint: Stop when the elbows reach 90 degrees of flexion, matching the source's standardized displacement.
execution.returnPhase: Extend both elbows together to full extension without turning the movement into a press.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep the upper arms at the reviewed 90-degree shoulder position while the elbows move.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep the torso supported and still, and maintain the same comfortable grip throughout the repetition.
disqualifyingCompensations: Moving the upper arms toward the torso turns the extension into a close-grip press.
Moving one elbow before the other leaves the simultaneous two-arm fixture.
Lowering beyond the source's 90-degree elbow-flexion endpoint changes the reviewed displacement.

execution.startingPosition: Stand at the high cable holding the straight bar with both palms down at shoulder width, keep the upper arms close to the torso, and lean slightly forward. Compare the entered load only on this same cable station and attachment.
execution.movement: Move only the forearms downward until both elbows reach full extension.
execution.endpoint: End with both elbows fully straight and the bar clear of the torso.
execution.returnPhase: Return through the full range while preserving the same upper-arm and torso positions.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep the upper arms perpendicular to the floor and the wrists neutral.
execution.supportAndPosture: Maintain the slight forward lean without using bodyweight to drive the bar.
disqualifyingCompensations: Leaning onto the bar changes the strict pushdown into a bodyweight-assisted push.
Moving the upper arms or allowing one arm to lead changes the reviewed two-arm elbow extension.

execution.startingPosition: Stand upright facing a cable set above your head. Hold one rope end in each hand with a neutral grip, brace your trunk, and keep both upper arms beside the torso. Compare the entered load only on this same cable station and attachment.
execution.movement: Extend both elbows together and press the rope toward the floor.
execution.endpoint: Finish with both elbows straight but not forcefully locked and the wrists still neutral.
execution.returnPhase: Allow both elbows to flex together under control until the upper arms would begin to drift forward.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep the shoulders, upper arms, forearms, and wrists in their starting alignment while the elbows move.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep the torso vertical and do not lean bodyweight onto the rope.
disqualifyingCompensations: Moving the upper arms forward turns the pushdown into a shoulder-driven cable movement.
Leaning onto the rope changes the strict pushdown into a bodyweight-assisted push.
Moving one arm before the other leaves the simultaneous two-arm fixture.

exercises.name: Life Fitness Pro 2 Seated Triceps Extension

execution.startingPosition: Compare the entered load only on this Life Fitness Pro 2 PSTE fixture. Sit with the hips against the lower-back pad, place both upper arms fully on the arm pad, align the elbows with the machine pivots, take the self-adjusting handles, position the feet under the foot bar, and hinge forward from the hips with the back straight.
execution.movement: Extend both elbows together while keeping both upper arms on the pad.
execution.endpoint: Finish at full elbow extension without lifting either upper arm from the pad.
execution.returnPhase: Allow both handles to return under control until the elbows are flexed at the start position.
execution.controlledJoints: Create the repetition only by straightening the elbows, letting the self-adjusting handles follow naturally without deliberately turning the forearms or bending the wrists.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep the hips against the lower-back pad, the back straight, both upper arms on the arm pad, and both feet under the foot bar.
disqualifyingCompensations: Lifting an upper arm from the pad changes the reviewed supported fixture.
Driving through the torso or feet adds body momentum.
Using another machine model or independent lever topology changes the fixture-specific load history.
